title: Number of Sites and One Supply Agreement per Site under Small Business Electricity Supply
content:
**Standard.** A business may enroll any number of its commercial sites in Small Business Electricity Supply; there is no limit on the number of small business agreements per customer. No other Small Business Electricity Supply agreement on the same site may be enrollment pending, active or drop pending when a new enrollment is submitted. A site may also not be enrolled while it is served under a Beacon Ridge commercial and industrial contract in pending or active status, because one premise has only one electricity supplier contract at a time.

## Basis of the check

- The check is made against the company's own records at the moment the new enrollment is submitted, not against what the caller says about the site.
- The object compared is the **site**: the new enrollment's site is matched to the site recorded on every existing small business agreement, and to the site of any Beacon Ridge commercial and industrial contract.
- The count of agreements a business already holds is not a ground for refusal: the number of agreements per customer has no limit.

## Status of another agreement on the same site

| Existing record on the same site | New Small Business Electricity Supply enrollment for that site |
|---|---|
| Small business agreement, enrollment pending | not permitted |
| Small business agreement, active | not permitted |
| Small business agreement, drop pending | not permitted |
| Beacon Ridge commercial and industrial contract, pending | not permitted |
| Beacon Ridge commercial and industrial contract, active | not permitted |

The table lists only the statuses the standard names; it says nothing about records in other statuses beyond what the standard itself states.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A restaurant group already holds eleven small business agreements, one per site, and asks to enroll a twelfth site that has no live agreement. The number of agreements it already holds does not stand in the way.
- A retailer asks to enroll a site whose earlier small business agreement is drop pending, the drop not yet having taken effect. The site still carries a drop-pending agreement, so the new enrollment is not permitted at that time.
